title: Consumer: Flipkart Refusing Refund on Shattered Screen Laptop (₹48,000)
input_narrative: On 12 October 2024, I purchased an Asus Vivobook laptop worth Rs 48,000 from Flipkart under Order OD328919102. When delivered on 15 October, the package was unsealed and the laptop display screen was completely shattered. I immediately raised a return request within 2 hours of delivery and uploaded unboxing photos. On 18 October, Flipkart rejected my return saying 'item damaged after delivery' and refused refund or replacement. Customer support is giving automated replies.

legal_assessment.summary_verdict: Refusal to refund or replace defective merchandise constitutes 'Deficiency of Service' under Section 2(11) and an 'Unfair Trade Practice' under Section 2(47) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.

applicable_statutes.plain_meaning: Any fault, imperfection, shortcoming or inadequacy in the quality, nature and manner of performance required by law or contract.
applicable_statutes.maximum_penalty_or_relief: Refund of amount paid, compensation for harassment/mental agony, and litigation costs.

applicable_statutes.plain_meaning: Deceptive practices including refusing refunds for defective goods, false guarantees, or charging above agreed price.
applicable_statutes.maximum_penalty_or_relief: Direction to discontinue unfair trade practice, issue full refund, and pay punitive damages.

applicable_statutes.official_title: Filing of Complaint before District Commission (e-Daakhil)
applicable_statutes.plain_meaning: Any consumer can file a complaint directly online via e-Daakhil for claims up to ₹50 Lakhs without needing to hire an advocate.
applicable_statutes.maximum_penalty_or_relief: Direct court order for full refund with interest and punitive compensation.

applicable_statutes.official_title: Statutory Period of Limitation for Recovery
applicable_statutes.plain_meaning: General civil recovery suits must be filed within 3 years from the date payment became due. Consumer complaints have a 2-year limitation (Section 69 CPA).
applicable_statutes.maximum_penalty_or_relief: Bar on judicial remedy if suit is not filed within the limitation period.

action_roadmap: Step 1: Send the drafted pre-litigation Legal Demand Notice to the e-commerce platform's Grievance Officer and seller.
Step 2: Register a grievance on the National Consumer Helpline portal (consumerhelpline.gov.in / dial 1915) citing the notice.
Step 3: If unresolved within 15 days, file a formal complaint online via e-Daakhil (edaakhil.nic.in) before the District Consumer Commission without hiring an advocate.
legal_assessment.realistic_outcome: E-commerce platforms typically initiate refund/replacement within 7-10 days of receiving a formal legal notice with NCH/e-Daakhil filing threat.
risks_and_caveats: Ensure you possess unboxing video, courier delivery receipt, and product serial number photos.
legal_assessment.legal_aid_option: Citizens with annual income below statutory limits (or women) are entitled to free state advocates via DLSA / NALSA.
